question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To set the Thames on fire

options.text: To do something remarkable or sensational

explanation: Set the Thames on fire = कोई बड़ा कमाल कर दिखाना (अक्सर निषेध में)। Example: He is hardworking, but he will never set the Thames on fire.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To be a law unto oneself

options.text: To follow one's own rules and ignore others'

explanation: A law unto oneself = अपने ही नियमों पर चलने वाला। Example: The old artist is a law unto himself.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To bear the brunt of

options.text: To suffer the main force of an attack or difficulty

explanation: Bear the brunt of = मुख्य आघात झेलना। Example: Small farmers bore the brunt of the drought.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To bask in reflected glory

options.text: To enjoy credit earned by someone else's success

explanation: Bask in reflected glory = दूसरे की कामयाबी की चमक में इठलाना। Example: The coach basked in the reflected glory of his pupil.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To bring someone to book

options.text: To punish someone or make him account for his actions
To give someone a book as a gift
To register someone in a library

explanation: Bring someone to book = जवाबदेह ठहराना, सज़ा दिलाना। Example: The corrupt officers were brought to book.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To carry the can

options.text: To take the blame for something others did too
To serve drinks at a party

explanation: Carry the can = दूसरों की ग़लती का दोष अपने सिर लेना। Example: The junior clerk had to carry the can for the error.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To cut a sorry figure

options.text: To make a poor or foolish impression
To reduce the cost of something

explanation: Cut a sorry figure = हास्यास्पद दिखना। Example: He cut a sorry figure at the party in torn clothes.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To cut one's coat according to one's cloth
explanation: Cut one's coat according to one's cloth = चादर देखकर पाँव पसारना। Example: Cut your coat according to your cloth, and you will not borrow.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To draw a veil over

options.text: To marry in a grand style
To cover a window with cloth
To avoid talking about something unpleasant

explanation: Draw a veil over = अप्रिय बात पर पर्दा डाल देना। Example: Let us draw a veil over the whole episode.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To end in smoke

options.text: To be cooked in a kitchen
To finish with a big fire

explanation: End in smoke = बेनतीजा रह जाना। Example: All his big plans ended in smoke.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To fall between two stools

options.text: To sit comfortably on a bench
To fail because one cannot choose between two options

explanation: Fall between two stools = दो नावों में पैर रखकर डूबना। Example: Hesitating between two jobs, he fell between two stools.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To feel the pinch

options.text: To suffer from a shortage of money

explanation: Feel the pinch = पैसे की तंगी महसूस करना। Example: Families are feeling the pinch of rising prices.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To gild the lily

options.text: To decorate something already beautiful, needlessly

explanation: Gild the lily = सुंदर चीज़ को व्यर्थ सजाना। Example: Adding jewellery to that dress would be gilding the lily.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To go through the mill

options.text: To undergo a hard training or difficult experience
To work in a flour mill

explanation: Go through the mill = कठिन दौर से गुज़रना। Example: Every recruit goes through the mill.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To harp on the same string

options.text: To play a musical instrument well
To keep talking about the same subject repeatedly

explanation: Harp on the same string = एक ही राग अलापना। Example: Stop harping on the same string about money.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To keep at bay

options.text: To prevent something unpleasant from coming close

explanation: Keep at bay = दूर रखना, पास न फटकने देना। Example: Garlic is believed to keep disease at bay.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To kill the fatted calf

options.text: To prepare a lavish feast to celebrate a return
To sacrifice an animal in secret

explanation: Kill the fatted calf = किसी के लौटने पर भव्य दावत करना। Example: The family killed the fatted calf when he came home.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To make light of
explanation: Make light of = हल्के में लेना। Example: Never make light of a doctor's warning.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To make short work of

options.text: To do a task very carefully
To finish or deal with something very quickly
To work for a short time only

explanation: Make short work of = झटपट निपटा देना। Example: The team made short work of the pending files.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To play havoc with

options.text: To play a game with friends
To cause great damage or disorder

explanation: Play havoc with = तबाही मचाना। Example: The storm played havoc with the crops.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To put a spoke in someone's wheel

options.text: To help someone start a business

explanation: Put a spoke in someone's wheel = किसी के काम में रोड़ा अटकाना। Example: His objection put a spoke in our wheel.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To queer the pitch

options.text: To spoil someone's plans in advance

explanation: Queer the pitch = पहले से किसी का खेल बिगाड़ देना। Example: A rival's rumour queered the pitch for our launch.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To rob Peter to pay Paul

options.text: To pay all debts at once
To take from one person in order to pay another

explanation: Rob Peter to pay Paul = एक से लेकर दूसरे को चुकाना। Example: Using one loan to repay another is robbing Peter to pay Paul.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To run to earth

options.text: To find something after a long search

explanation: Run to earth = लंबी खोज के बाद पकड़ लेना। Example: The police ran the thief to earth in a village.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To take to one's heels
explanation: Take to one's heels = सिर पर पाँव रखकर भाग जाना। Example: The boys took to their heels when the guard shouted.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To weigh anchor

options.text: To stop a ship in port
To raise the anchor and set sail

explanation: Weigh anchor = लंगर उठाकर जहाज़ रवाना करना। Example: The ship weighed anchor at dawn.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To be in clover

options.text: To live in comfort and luxury
To be very lucky in a game

explanation: In clover = ऐश-आराम में रहना। Example: After his lottery win, he lived in clover.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To be tarred with the same brush

options.text: To work for the same boss
To share the same faults as another

explanation: Tarred with the same brush = एक ही थैली के चट्टे-बट्टे होना। Example: Don't blame all of them; they are not tarred with the same brush.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A thorn in one's side

options.text: A constant source of trouble or annoyance

explanation: A thorn in one's side = लगातार परेशानी की जड़। Example: The noisy neighbour is a thorn in my side.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To scrape through

options.text: To succeed or pass by a very narrow margin

explanation: Scrape through = मुश्किल से पास हो जाना। Example: He scraped through the exam with 36 marks.
